deltas.delta: All three web3_clientVersion queries to mainnet.optimism.io on 2026-11-26 returned op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown, the unversioned build; the versioned v2.8.1 build that answered one query in three on 2026-11-25 did not answer. Every vector and script above therefore ran on the unversioned build.

Lagoon now has dates. Upgrade 22 activates it on OP Sepolia, Unichain Sepolia, Ink Sepolia and Soneium Minato on 10 December 2026 and on OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink and Soneium on 11 January 2027 16:00:01 UTC (timestamp 1799683201), subject to Optimism governance (proposal 2 December, veto period ends 9 December). Interop is turned on between OP Mainnet and Unichain only. The node release named for it is op-reth v2.10.0, whose op-revm files equal those of the rc.4 build these chains run and map LAGOON to the Osaka instruction set (cycle 22 reading), so the day-one instruction table for the PoolManager bytecode is unchanged. OP Mainnet and Unichain then move their respected proof to the ZK dispute game on 14 January 2027.

profiles.summary: Transaction boundaries hold on every handler read, including the builder path that failed on Base in June 2026. Lagoon adds refund settlement outside frames and deposits-only replacement of blocks with invalid interop messages.

deltas.delta: The Base outage of 25 and 26 June 2026 (116 and 20 minutes) came from the block builder keeping the journal of a transaction that failed validation, so the warm account and slot set of an excluded transaction changed the gas of the next one and the sealed block was rejected by every validator. The fix (base/base PR 3806) adds discard_tx in the non-deposit branch of catch_error. The same discard is present in every handler that this unit's clients and builders pin: Base v1.5.6 (handler.rs:385-387) and v1.6.0-rc.3, op-revm at op-reth v2.8.0 (Zora), v2.8.1, v2.10.0-rc.4 and v2.10.0, the two optimism revisions World Chain v2.8.2 pins, and the revision op-rbuilder pins (handler.rs discard_and_surface_error). A validation failure stops before any frame runs, so no TSTORE of the failed transaction could have been carried; the fault reached gas only.

From Lagoon, a sequenced block on OP Mainnet or Unichain that holds an executing message whose initiating message is not valid is replaced by a deposits-only block at the same height, which removes every user transaction in it. Deposits cannot execute interop messages: CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage reverts when the base fee is above zero and the gas price is zero.

From Lagoon, a block may end in a post-execution transaction (type 0x7D) built by the sequencer. It runs no EVM code, carries Sequencer-Defined Metering gas refunds, and each refund is settled after the refunded transaction's frame finishes and before its state is committed: the sender is credited and the block beneficiary, base fee vault and operator fee vault are debited. No balance changes inside a frame, so msg.value and the balances read between sync and settle are unaffected.

profiles.summary: Gas refunds under Sequencer-Defined Metering change fees only.

deltas.delta: Sequencer-Defined Metering lets the sequencer refund gas of chosen transactions after Lagoon; Unichain plans a refund policy that makes swaps on the Uniswap protocol cheaper. Refunds move fees between the sender and the fee recipients only, and verifiers do not run the policy.

profiles.summary: Interop predeploys are still empty proxies; their release sources give the PoolManager no payable or token entry point.

deltas.delta: On 2026-11-26 the proxies at 0x4200..0022 to 0x25, 0x29, 0x2a, 0x30 and 0x31 still have an empty EIP-1967 implementation slot on OP Mainnet, Unichain, OP Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia; 0x2c (ConditionalDeployer) and 0x2d (L2DevFeatureFlags) have implementations. The op-contracts v10.0.0 sources of CrossL2Inbox, L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger, SuperchainETHBridge, ETHLiquidity, NativeAssetLiquidity, LiquidityController, ConditionalDeployer, L2DevFeatureFlags, ChainConfig and UndeliveredMessageExporter have no receive or fallback function and no transfer or balanceOf selector. SuperchainETHBridge.relayETH and refundETH pay through SafeSend, a contract that self-destructs to the recipient, so ETH relayed to the PoolManager arrives without a call. At activation ETHLiquidity is funded with a deposit minting 2^128 - 1 wei.

findings.title: After Lagoon an unsafe reorg on OP Mainnet or Unichain replaces dependent blocks on the other chain with deposits-only blocks
findings.difference: From 11 January 2027 OP Mainnet and Unichain form an interop dependency set. The sequencer may include an executing message that consumes an initiating message from an unsafe block of the other chain, and a block whose executing message turns out invalid is replaced by a block that holds only its deposits.
findings.mechanism: An account emits a log on OP Mainnet in an unsafe block and, within seconds, sends a Unichain transaction that executes it; other users' swaps, liquidity removals and takes against the Unichain PoolManager follow in the same Unichain block. If the OP Mainnet block is later reorganised (sequencer equivocation, a batch not posted within the sequencing window, or an L1 reorg), cross-chain validation marks the executing message invalid and derivation replaces the whole Unichain block with a deposits-only block. Each removed unlock is atomic (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so the PoolManager's balances and deltas stay consistent; what disappears is every user transaction of that block, which users and integrators may already have treated as done from the unsafe receipt.
findings.impact: No PoolManager funds move or freeze. Users whose exits sat in a replaced block must resend them; bridges, exchanges or solvers that released value on the strength of an unsafe receipt of a swap or take can be left short. The width of the effect is one block per invalid message, and a cascade is possible when the replaced block itself held initiating messages consumed on the other chain.
findings.preconditions: Lagoon active with interop between OP Mainnet and Unichain, a sequencer policy that admits messages from unsafe remote blocks, and an unsafe reorg on the remote chain. The last needs the sequencer, the batcher operator or an Ethereum reorg; an ordinary account cannot cause it, and deposits cannot carry executing messages.
findings.mitigations: Integrators should treat only safe heads as final for value released off chain on these two chains after Lagoon. Sequencers can restrict executing messages to safe remote blocks. Nothing in core needs to change.

sources.supports: invalid executing messages invalidate a block, which is replaced by a deposits-only block; deposits are prevented from executing messages
the sequencer may include executing messages with any level of confirmation safety, at higher risk of an invalid block
interop between OP Mainnet and Unichain activates with Lagoon on 11 January 2027, subject to governance

findings.title: A transaction that failed validation in Base's block builder halted every exit on Base for 116 minutes in June 2026, and the fault is fixed in every builder and node handler read
findings.difference: Ethereum clients drop the journal of a transaction that fails validation. Base's builder kept it, so the warm accounts and slots of the excluded transaction leaked into the next one.
findings.mechanism: On 25 June 2026 an invalid transaction reached the builder of block 47806543 and failed validation. The builder did not clear the journal, the next valid transaction ran against the dirty access set and was charged different gas, and the receipts root of the sealed block differed from what validators computed. Validators rejected the block and the chain stopped at 47806542 for 116 minutes, and for 20 minutes on 26 June. Any account can send a transaction that fails validation in the builder; the PR's tests use a sender with code and a stale nonce. Because validation fails before any frame runs, no TSTORE of the failed transaction existed, so the PoolManager's lock, deltas and synced currency (src/libraries/Lock.sol, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol) could not have been carried into the next transaction. Had a leak reached state, validators would have rejected that block too. The fix adds discard_tx to the non-deposit branch of catch_error (base/base PR 3806), present in v1.5.6 at handler.rs:385-387 and in v1.6.0-rc.3; op-revm, which the other six chains and op-rbuilder use, discards the journal on both the transaction error and other error paths, and revm's inspector run path calls the same catch_error.
findings.impact: While halted no PoolManager exit on Base could be included, so every liquidity provider and claim holder on Base was frozen for the duration. No funds were lost and no wrong state was accepted.
findings.preconditions: A builder whose error path keeps the journal. None of the builds read today has that fault.
findings.mitigations: None needed in core. Deployers on single-sequencer chains should expect temporary halts triggered by public transactions and keep withdrawals free of deadlines shorter than such halts.

sources.supports: root cause: stale journal after a transaction validation failure; block 47806543 rejected by validators; 116 and 20 minute halts
the fix adds discard_tx in catch_error and tests EIP-3607 and nonce failures
the running build carries the fix at lines 385-387
the op-revm revision op-rbuilder pins discards the journal on every non-deposit error

cleared.check: Battery (99,985 vectors) and targeted set (85,544 vectors) at the builds answering on 2026-11-26, with OP Mainnet's endpoint answering only its unversioned build: MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, comparisons, JUMPI, KECCAK256, MCOPY, CALLDATALOAD and the FullMath, divRoundingUp and BalanceDelta sequences.
cleared.result: Every vector returns the specified word on all seven chains; 0 mismatches and 0 errors. The libraries that consume these opcodes (FullMath, BitMath, TickMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) therefore get the specified inputs.

cleared.check: Script sets 1 and 2 on the deployed PoolManager bytecode at today's builds.
cleared.result: Set 1: 248 of 250 scripts identical to the Ethereum reference on every chain, 0 different; the reference endpoint returned an error for the other two, so they were not compared. Set 2: 300 of 300 identical on every chain.

cleared.check: Mined swaps since the cycle 22 windows: tick relation, single-step formulas and full Pool.swap replay from parent-block state.
cleared.result: 18,699 swaps all satisfy the tick relation (6 on OP Mainnet sit on a boundary, as Pool.sol:430-431 allows), 15,358 paired swaps match a single-step outcome or were replayed, and all 107 multi-step and crossed swaps replayed through the loop match to the unit, the longest with 11 steps on Zora.

cleared.check: Base v1.6.0-rc.2 and rc.3: interpreter, integer library, instruction table and evm2 wiring (lead L-983).
cleared.result: rc.3 keeps the rc.1 pins and byte identical EVM crate files; evm2 rev 9b037449 has no dependent other than base-common-evm2, which is not wired into the node. Nothing to rerun yet.

cleared.check: conduit-op-reth v2.5.2, the release after Zora's running v2.5.1.
cleared.result: Only the conduit crates change; op-revm, revm, revm-interpreter and ruint pins are the same.

cleared.check: Does any handler or builder on these chains keep the journal of a failed transaction, the Base June 2026 fault class, so that a TSTORE, a warm set or a partial write of one transaction reaches the next (assumption A1 for the unlock flag, deltas and synced currency).
cleared.result: No. Base v1.5.6 and v1.6.0-rc.3 call discard_tx for every non-deposit error; op-revm at op-reth v2.8.0, v2.8.1, v2.10.0-rc.4, v2.10.0, World Chain's two pinned revisions and op-rbuilder's pinned revision call discard_and_surface_error for transaction and other errors, and revm-inspector 43.0.3 inspect_run routes errors through the same catch_error.

cleared.check: Lagoon post-execution transaction and Sequencer-Defined Metering: can the refund settlement change the PoolManager's balance or what a frame sees between sync and settle.
cleared.result: No. The 0x7D transaction is not executed as EVM code; each refund credits tx.from and debits the block beneficiary and fee vaults after the refunded transaction's frame ends and before commit. The PoolManager is never tx.from or a fee recipient, and src/PoolManager.sol:349-364 reads balances only inside frames.

cleared.check: Lagoon interop: can a relayed message make the PoolManager act for someone else, and can a forced-inclusion deposit execute a message or see transient storage of a sequenced transaction.
cleared.result: L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.relayMessage calls any target except two messengers with msg.sender equal to the messenger, so a message to the PoolManager can only call unlock, which calls unlockCallback on the messenger and reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:104-110), or functions that need no lock and act on the messenger's own claims. CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage reverts for deposits. Deposits run first in a block, each in its own transaction, and op-revm clears transient storage at commit.

cleared.check: Native and token calls from the PoolManager to the Lagoon predeploys in the op-contracts v10.0.0 sources (leads L-417 and L-892): P1 native take with empty calldata, P2 transfer, P3 balanceOf.
cleared.result: None of the ten predeploy sources has a receive or fallback function or a transfer or balanceOf selector, so P1 reverts at the proxy's delegate call, and P2 and P3 revert; no payout is stranded and no balance can be synced. ETH that SuperchainETHBridge relays to the PoolManager arrives by SafeSend self-destruct, and native settle credits only msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354), so it becomes an unclaimable surplus that no account can take.

cleared.check: Lead L-1048: which blocks can be reorganised after public RPC served them, and can an ordinary account trigger it, for example with a forced-inclusion deposit.
cleared.result: Only blocks between the safe and unsafe head (13 seconds on Base to 3,302 seconds on Zora at the time of the query), and only through sequencer equivocation, a batch missing the sequencing window or an L1 reorg. A deposit is placed by derivation at the start of an L2 block whose L1 origin includes it and does not invalidate earlier sequenced blocks; after Lagoon deposits cannot execute interop messages. In the one halt of the year found (Base, June 2026), validators never accepted the bad block, so nothing served was removed.

leads.question: After Lagoon activates on OP Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia on 10 December 2026, do the implementations installed behind 0x4200..0022 to 0x25, 0x29, 0x2a, 0x30 and 0x31 equal the op-contracts v10.0.0 sources read here, and does a native take from the PoolManager address to each revert?
leads.why: The clearance rests on the release sources; a deployed implementation with a payable fallback would strand a caller's payout (F-048 shape).

leads.question: Which refund policy does Unichain's sequencer apply under Sequencer-Defined Metering, does it select transactions by PoolManager calls or logs, and can an ordinary account collect refunds above what it paid for gas?
leads.why: Refunds move fees only, but a policy keyed on PoolManager activity gives a reason to send empty or circular PoolManager calls; the refund bound evmGasUsed limits it to the sender's own fee.

leads.question: op-rbuilder's tagged v0.4.14 and main pin revm 41.0.0 and an optimism revision older than the nodes' revm 43.0.3, and no tagged builder release names Lagoon support. Which builder release will produce 0x7D blocks on these chains, and do its handler and instruction table match op-reth v2.10.0?
leads.why: A builder that computes differently from the nodes halts the chain (the Base June 2026 shape), which freezes exits without loss.

leadResults.answer: Not run: the kona-client toolchain and Cannon emulator are still not available here. New fact: Upgrade 22 requires a new cannon64-kona-interop prestate built from a Lagoon kona-client release, not yet published, and OP Mainnet and Unichain plan to make the ZK dispute game (type 10) their respected game on 14 January 2027, so the 0x03e5a548 prestate stops being the one that settles new withdrawals there; Ink keeps a Cannon kona game. The question should be retargeted to the Lagoon prestate once its hash is published.

Everest is still Planning with no date on Sepolia or mainnet (docs.base.org/upgrades/everest/overview). The newest tag, v1.6.0-rc.3, has an eip8130.rs byte identical to rc.1, so the cycle 22 reading of the phase loop holds; type 0x79 still cannot be simulated.

Lagoon is now dated: 10 December 2026 on OP Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia, 11 January 2027 on mainnet. On 2026-11-26 the implementation slots of 0x22 to 0x25, 0x29, 0x2a, 0x30 and 0x31 are still empty on all four networks. The op-contracts v10.0.0 sources give none of them a receive, fallback, transfer or balanceOf, so all sixteen call shapes are expected to revert; the installed code must be read after 10 December.

Same state as L-892. From the release sources: ETHLiquidity has burn, mint and fund (payable, with a selector) and setPaused; SuperchainETHBridge has sendETH, relayETH and refundETH; neither has receive or fallback, so no call shape the PoolManager can send is accepted. Confirm against installed bytecode after the Sepolia activation.
Base v1.6.0-rc.3 still links evm2 rev 9b037449 only through base-common-evm2, which nothing depends on and whose README says it is not wired into the node; nothing to read or rerun yet.

The Zora census did not finish in this session. Base and World Chain endpoints refuse wide log ranges (request limit, head range error), so they were not extended; the source reading of cycle 22 stands for them, and this cycle found the same discard on every error path of the builders.

Public RPC serves blocks up to the unsafe head, 13 seconds ahead of safe on Base and 3,302 seconds on Zora at the time of query. Those blocks can be replaced only by sequencer equivocation, a batch missing the sequencing window or an L1 reorg; an ordinary account cannot trigger any of them, and a forced-inclusion deposit runs first in its block in its own transient scope and after Lagoon cannot execute interop messages. No unsafe reorg of served blocks was found in the past year; Base's June 2026 halt left the bad block unaccepted. New operator-level finding: after Lagoon an unsafe reorg on OP Mainnet or Unichain replaces dependent blocks on the other chain with deposits-only blocks.
